analysis.title: Europe and US Conviction Names (Reporting w/c 26 Oct)
key_insights: UBS expects Orange 3Q26 (reports 27 Oct) to show organic resilience across France, Spain, MEA, Poland and Belgium. Orange has raised guidance twice year to date. UBS OCF for 2028 is EUR 5.5bn vs consensus EUR 5.2bn, so management could upgrade its 2028 CMD targets.

Adyen (reports 28 Oct): UBS says organic growth near 20% would support confidence in ~20% net revenue growth in 2027. Shares fell in September on EU de minimis rules, macro pressure and agentic commerce concerns. Crowding has moved from a notable long to neutral. Options imply a move of about 10%.

Campari (reports 28 Oct): UBS forecasts Q3 organic sales +3.8%, 50bp above consensus, driven by aperitifs. European aperitifs grew 5.2% Q3-to-date vs a 9.0% decline for the rest of the portfolio. UBS sees FY26 gross-margin guidance as conservative and forecasts 80bp of EBIT-margin expansion. Short interest is about 21 days to cover and 18% of free float.

Epiroc (Sell, reports 28 Oct): UBS forecasts Q3 outcomes of +3%/-3%/-5% vs consensus and expects a mildly negative catalyst. Adjusted EBIT is forecast 5% below consensus on operating leverage. Orders are above consensus, revenue below.

GSK (Neutral, reports 28 Oct): UBS is cautious on initial momentum for Blenrep and Exdensur and sees potential for growth to disappoint at 3Q. Exdensur momentum is expected from 4Q26, and Blenrep management is following a 'go slow before going big' approach because of ocular toxicity.

Glencore (reports 29 Oct): UBS upgraded to Buy in late September, citing Q3 as a catalyst. UBS is 19% above consensus on FY26 Marketing EBIT and 25% above on FY27, and sees ~15% upside to consensus 2027 EBITDA at spot commodity prices. The commodity basket is up ~20% YTD.

Magnum Ice Cream (reports 29 Oct): UBS forecasts Q3 organic sales growth of 5.3% vs Visible Alpha consensus 3.7%, with volumes +3.7% vs consensus +2.1%, helped by European weather. Short interest was 14.0% in late September, nearly 40 days to cover. UBS forecasts FY26 OSG of 5.1% vs consensus 4.4%.

Prysmian (reports 29 Oct): UBS forecasts 3Q26 adjusted EBITDA of EUR 824m, 5% above consensus, led by Digital Solutions on repriced data-centre fibre contracts. A strong quarter could lift FY26 EBITDA guidance to EUR 2.9-3.0bn from EUR 2.8-2.9bn. UBS is 4%, 10% and 10% above consensus on EBITDA for 2026-28.

SPIE (reports 30 Oct): UBS sees Q3 as a potential inflection, with organic revenue growth of +3.2% y/y vs +3.1% consensus, after +3.0% in Q2 and -0.9% in Q1. Shares are -15% YTD and -19% since the July peak, at 12x 2027 PE. Crowding has moved from over 1 s.d. long to neutral.

Freeport-McMoRan (reports 27 Oct): UBS calls it one of the better second-derivative AI trades. Data center power generation accounts for 900kt of copper demand in 2025 and 1.55Mt by 2030, or 15-20% of copper demand growth.

Corning (reports 27 Oct): UBS is 20% above consensus with a 40% EPS CAGR through 2030. The debate is whether investors over-penalize slower fiber/CPO/photonics timing despite long-term offtake agreements.
HCA Healthcare (reports 27 Oct): UBS sees AI-driven productivity gains as a catalyst to re-rate the stock above its historical 8-10x EV/EBITDA range.
Johnson Controls (reports 27 Oct): The debate is whether 2027 estimates are too low if low-double-digit growth and 40% incremental margins hold. The stock trades at 27x EPS, a 10% premium to XLI.
Nucor (Neutral, reports 27 Oct): Trades at 7.1x 2027 EBITDA vs 8.5x in January. UBS cites import parities supporting pricing and limited energy cost risk.
Royal Caribbean (reports 27 Oct): Per diems are up 24% vs 2019 and supply growth remains below pre-COVID levels.

Repligen (reports 27 Oct): UBS is incrementally positive on MFN/equipment tailwinds, China growth, the BioLife deal, new modalities including mRNA, and upside to sell-side expectations. It remains a top pick.

S&P Global (reports 27 Oct): UBS says AI disruption risk is overstated because 83% of Market Intelligence operating income is insulated. The implied valuation for Market Intelligence is 7x vs FDS at 12x.
Teradyne (reports 27 Oct): UBS cites leverage to AI ASIC test, share gains from Advantest and an inflecting robotics business tied to Amazon.
Amphenol (reports 28 Oct): UBS says AI data center growth remains strong, guidance is conservative, and higher-margin AI sales are producing strong incremental margins.

Biogen (reports 28 Oct): UBS cites Phase III catalysts in SLE, CLE and AMR, TB-03 in Alzheimer's, TAU entering Phase III, and positive Phase II BTK inhibitor data in MS. The APLS acquisition bridges revenue growth through 2030.
C.H. Robinson (reports 28 Oct): UBS views AI as more likely a productivity lever than a risk for large freight brokers.
Chipotle (reports 28 Oct): UBS sees mid-single-digit same-store sales as achievable and store growth accelerating to 10%. The stock trades at 34x next year's PE vs 45x historically.
Carvana (reports 28 Oct): UBS sees market share growing from 1.5% to 4% by 2030 and EBITDA growing at a 25% CAGR through 2030.
HF Sinclair (reports 28 Oct): UBS expects above mid-cycle earnings through 1H28, with at least 50% of adjusted net income returned via buybacks and dividends.
Ford (reports 28 Oct): UBS sees a path to over $2 EPS in 2027 and $3+ later in the decade.
GE Vernova (reports 28 Oct): UBS remains positive on multi-year earnings growth and keeps a $1,400 price target.

Microsoft (reports 28 Oct): UBS calls the EPS preview positive. It sees a 47% Azure growth bogey and a 46-47% guide as achievable, with M365 upside from Copilot usage-based pricing. Valuation is 23x CY27 non-GAAP EPS.
Nextpower (reports 28 Oct): UBS says it is capturing 45X advanced manufacturing tax credits, and acquisitions have tripled its TAM.
O'Reilly Auto (reports 28 Oct): Comps grew 6%, trends strengthened into 3Q, and guidance is conservative.
Amazon (reports 29 Oct): UBS calls it a 'coiled spring' for EPS upside, since costs are in numbers but revenue upside is not. The stock trades at 12x EBITDA and 21x P/E.
Bunge (reports 29 Oct): UBS says the earnings and cash flow benefit from 100% SRE reallocation is underappreciated and expects upward revisions through 2027.
Bristol-Myers Squibb (reports 29 Oct): The Phase III milvexian Afib readout (YE26) carries a 35-50% probability of success and a ±15% stock move. Valuation of 9x P/E could re-rate to 12x+ on success.
BorgWarner (reports 29 Oct): UBS sees non-auto at 30% of EBIT by 2030 and a 19% EPS CAGR through 2030, supporting a re-rating.
CRH (reports 29 Oct): UBS cites best-in-class earnings growth, US infrastructure exposure, and potential S&P 500 inclusion as a catalyst.
Entegris (reports 29 Oct): UBS expects an AI-driven edge upgrade cycle and a new CEO who will cut fixed costs.
First Solar (reports 29 Oct): UBS cites 45X tax credits, tariffs, the Section 232 polysilicon investigation and tripling of US manufacturing capacity.
TechnipFMC (reports 29 Oct): UBS initiates at Buy. Subsea 2.0 is 80% of new orders but 50% of FY27 Subsea revenue. FY28 EBITDA is 5% above consensus and FY27 Subsea orders are expected above $11B.
Illumina (reports 29 Oct): UBS expects an in-line to modest Q3 beat and a reiterated guide. It models FY26 organic growth of 4.7% and EPS of $5.38, and FY27 organic growth of 8.6% and EPS of $6.26.
Ionis (reports 29 Oct): UBS assumes coverage at Buy with an $88 PT. It models 2035 Tryngolza sales of $3.6BN vs $3.1BN consensus. Shares trade at ~2.8x EV/discounted sales vs ~4.4x for peers.
Linde (reports 29 Oct): UBS sees space fuel growing from $350m to $2.9B by 2030, or 6.5% of sales, adding 1%+ ppts annually to sales growth.
Eli Lilly (reports 29 Oct): UBS expects a beat-and-raise led by Zepbound. It models US Orforglipron launch sales of $1.5B vs consensus $1B, and a 30x multiple on $40 EPS in 2027-28.
Trane Tech (reports 29 Oct): UBS sees operating profits beating consensus in each of 2026-2028 and positive revisions in 2026.
West Pharma (reports 29 Oct): UBS cites biologics exposure, a rising high-value product mix and Annex 1-driven upgrades.
nVent (reports 30 Oct): UBS raises 2027 sales and EPS forecasts to 17-19% above consensus. It forecasts 25% organic growth vs consensus 16%, and 2027 EPS of $6.91 vs consensus $5.82.
Regeneron (reports 30 Oct): UBS assumes coverage at Buy with a $978 PT. The stock trades at ~12x 2027 P/E vs 16x for peers, and UBS sees ~25% upside as pipeline programs advance.

risk_factors: Adyen: agentic commerce implications, EU de minimis regulation and macro pressure.
Epiroc: manufacturing output too high relative to the scale of the business, creating margin and cash flow risk.
GSK: slow launch momentum for Blenrep (ocular toxicity) and Exdensur (6-month dosing and reimbursement).
Glencore: commodity price weakness or softer marketing earnings.
Bristol-Myers Squibb: the milvexian Afib readout has only a 35-50% probability of success.
vol_and_positioning: Implied earnings moves (UBS Derivatives Strategy), with multiples of the 1M realised average: Orange 2.4 (1.6x), Adyen 10.1 (5.8x), Campari 1.9 (1.4x), Epiroc 5.1 (2.6x), GSK 3.4 (2.1x), Glencore 2.8 (1.6x), Magnum 4.2 (2.3x), Prysmian 2.4 (0.9x), SPIE 4.1 (3.1x).
US implied earnings moves: Repligen 11.4, Teradyne 11.3, Carvana 12.0, Nextpower 11.6, Entegris 10.1, Illumina 9.3, West Pharma 9.6 (7.1x realised), Corning 7.0, First Solar 7.7, nVent 7.8.
Adyen: crowding shrank from a notable long to neutral this year.
Campari short interest is about 21 days to cover and 18% of free float, which could amplify a positive surprise.
Magnum Ice Cream short interest was 14.0% across listings in late September, nearly 40 days to cover.
SPIE crowding moved from over 1 s.d. long to neutral, with short interest over 9 days to cover.
geopolitical: US trade protectionism, tariffs and the Section 232 investigation into polysilicon, plus Trump executive order enforcement on foreign entities of concern, cited as supports for First Solar
EU de minimis regulation cited as a pressure on Adyen shares in September
Chinese safety-related production disruptions supporting met coal prices, cited for Glencore
